answers.question: Has PMMA been tested for fire near the atmosphere of a lunar habitat (34% oxygen, 56.5 kPa, 1/6 g)?
answers.answer: No source-table row in this collection matches that atmosphere. Of 90 PMMA rows, all 90 are microgravity and none is at 1/6 g. The 41 rows that state oxygen span 14.2 to 22.2 percent, never 34, and no row states or infers a pressure below 101.3 kPa, against 56.5. The nearest row, PSI-25:1, is 22.2 percent O2 at an inferred 101.3 kPa. The lunar-gravity table here covers Mylar, Ultem and Nomex, not PMMA.
answers.limits: This covers only the rows and documents in this collection, so absence here does not mean NASA never studied PMMA at lunar gravity, and nothing here describes the safety of any material or atmosphere.

answers.question: What do the NASA rows say about how gravity changes how far a material burns?
answers.answer: In this collection, burn length at both gravity levels is read from one source table, SAFFIRE-II (PSI-99), nine rows. Eight are comparable: five burned further in normal gravity, none further in microgravity, three the same; one is not comparable. Only two rows give numbers at both levels: PSI-99:2 records about 0 in microgravity against 7.6 cm in normal gravity, while PSI-99:3 records about 0 at both. The other comparisons rely on the word "Complete", read as the full 29 cm sample length.
answers.limits: Nine samples from one experiment, comparing microgravity with normal gravity only; no row in this collection tests the Moon or Mars, and the pattern does not rate any material or support a general law.

answers.question: At what ambient oxygen do droplet flames stop going out on their own in the FLEX tests?
answers.answer: In this collection's FLEX droplet table, extinction last appears at 30% ambient oxygen, in two methanol source-table rows, PSI-69:30 and PSI-69:45. All 9 rows above 30%, every one at 34%, ended in disruption or completion, none in extinction. Extinction shares fall as oxygen rises: 103 of 115 rows at 18% or less, 63 of 91 over 18% to 22%, and 20 of 59 over 22% to 30%. These are counts, not a sharp threshold.
answers.limits: These are liquid-droplet source-table rows in microgravity, not cabin-material results; only one NASA table is read, rows above 30% are few (9, all at 34%) and fuel and diluent mixes differ, so absence of extinction there is not a measured limit.

answers.question: What did NASA measure about material flammability at lunar and Martian gravity?
answers.answer: One NASA report, held outside the source-table rows, lists limiting oxygen for three materials. Lunar-gravity MOC* was 14.1, 19.9 and 19.9 percent O2 for Mylar G, Ultem 1000 and Nomex HT90-40, against 20.0, 23.0 and 22.1 at 1g. Martian MOC* was 17.0, 21.1 and 19.0. Stated lunar margins were -5.75, -2.8 and -2.35, and recomputing them agreed. In this collection, 0 of 1,989 source-table rows are at partial gravity.
answers.limits: The values come from three materials in drop-tower tests whose low-g criterion (flame survival over the drop time) differs from the 1g criterion (NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 burn length), so they are report values, not source-table rows or a cabin rating, and nothing here says any material or atmosphere is safe.

answers.question: For the space station cabin, which questions have nearby evidence, and what is assumed about pressure?
answers.answer: For the station preset (21% O2, 101.4 kPa, microgravity), 3 of 45 material-by-concern questions have nearby source-table rows in this collection, all for prevention: PMMA with 16 rows, SIBAL with 6, Nomex with 2. All 24 matched rows carry a facility-inferred pressure of 101.3 kPa, assumed as the nominal glovebox value; none reports a measured pressure. Another 21 questions have no source in this collection. Limits: rows are source-table rows within 1 O2 point and 5 kPa tolerances, not independent experiments, and a match is coverage, not a safety finding.
answers.limits: Counts hold only for the station preset values in presets.json and VESTA's matching tolerances. They describe evidence coverage in this collection, not what NASA has studied or whether any cabin material is safe. The 21 questions with no source mean absent from this collection. No NTRS document in partialg-sources.json bears on this question, so none is cited.

answers.question: Which cabin materials have no source at all in this collection for fire suppression?
answers.answer: Of 15 cabin materials in this collection, 8 have no suppression-tagged source-table row. Seven of them also have no suppression finding: Kapton, Teflon, lampwick, Pyrell, dibutyl phthalate, PMMA plus Nomex, and silicone rubber. Their 96 source-table rows are tagged only prevention or detection, for example PSI-101:1 (Kapton, detection). The eighth, silicone, has 26 rows tagged only prevention or detection (for example PSI-99:1, prevention) and one suppression finding, SAFFIRE-028, a normal-gravity ground test that names silicone in its text but is not linked to a material id. The other seven materials do have suppression rows; PMMA has 48, including PSI-26:2, and SOLIDS-008 is the only suppression finding linked to a material id.
answers.limits: No source means absent from this collection, not unstudied by NASA; the 8 materials still have rows for other concerns, and the seven others being present says nothing about adequacy. The status cells count silicone as never tested because they link findings by material id only; SAFFIRE-028 is a ground-test finding, not a cabin-material suppression result in microgravity. Liquid-droplet findings are excluded as cabin-material results.

answers.question: What evidence does the collection hold for Nomex?
answers.answer: In this collection, Nomex has 9 source-table rows, all microgravity: PSI-25:23 to PSI-25:25 (BASS-II) and six BASS rows from PSI-26:14 to PSI-26:58, plus one PMMA-and-Nomex row, PSI-99:7. Among the nine Nomex rows, only PSI-25:23 and PSI-25:24 carry numeric outcomes; PSI-99:7 records a burn time of 140 s, with the Nomex spread rate printed as n/a. Findings SOLIDS-045 and SAFFIRE-101 report samples that did not ignite; SOLIDS-018 reports a 2 cm sample that burned. One NASA table prints Nomex HT90-40 ULOI as 23.5 at 1g and 23.0 at 0g. Detection has no rows.
answers.limits: All rows are ISS or Cygnus flight rows with sparse conditions; for the nine ISS rows pressure is not recorded and is inferred (101.3 kPa), and PSI-99:7 has no pressure at all. Absence means absent from this collection, not unstudied.

answers.question: Which recorded conditions does VESTA show but not use when it decides a row is nearby?
answers.answer: VESTA calls a row nearby using only gravity class, oxygen within 1.0 point and pressure within 5.0 kPa. At the station preset (21% O2, 101.4 kPa, microgravity) it finds 24 nearby source-table rows; all 24 have pressure inferred from a nominal glovebox assumption (101.3 kPa), not recorded in the row. All 24 also record fan, air or flow-restrictor settings, which have no unit and are not compared. Specimen size is recorded in 22 rows and a thickness named in the size text in 9, for example PSI-25:21 (1 cm wide, 200 micron thick PMMA). A size such as PSI-25:6 (2 cm; 0.1 mm PMMA film) is recorded but not named as a thickness. Recorded flow velocity and ignition entries appear in 0 of the 24.
answers.limits: Counts are for the station preset and the prevention concern only; the spacecraft, lunar-base, rover and mars-base presets have 0 nearby rows here, and fields are recorded text in this collection, not tested for effect on any outcome. "Named thickness" means the size text itself says thick.

answers.question: How good is the oxygen model for droplet extinction, compared with simple baselines?
answers.answer: In this collection's FLEX droplet table, 224 dated source-table rows were held out one test day at a time (66 days). A logistic model on oxygen and fuel got 179 right. The majority baseline got 150, the same-fuel majority 128, and a single oxygen cut 164. Against the majority baseline the gap is +12.9 points (+2.5 to +23.4). Against the oxygen cut it is +6.7 points (−2.5 to +16.1), which includes zero.
answers.limits: This is an internal check on one liquid-droplet table; test-day rows are not independent, 50 undated rows are left out, and the result says nothing about cabin materials.
